clue.text: Animal research facility upset about mating period

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the flipped facility wraps round the period
in a down clue upset turns things over; here it flips the facility's letters end to end

parts.note: a lab is a research facility
the rut is the season when deer and similar animals mate

explanation.surface: Activists object to an animal research lab that interferes with breeding seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal research facility' reads as one phrase, but 'Animal' is split off as the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal as an adjective describes savage, beastlike behaviour, which is what brutal conduct is.

clue.text: Gross author, not popular

indicators.note: not tells the solver to take away the word for popular from the name

parts.note: Ian Rankin, the Scottish crime novelist
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A disgusting writer whom nobody likes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Rankin writes the Rebus detective novels; dropping IN from his surname leaves RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and gross are synonyms as adjectives meaning flagrant or foul-smelling, as in rank stupidity.

clue.text: Urinal fitted with tap cover

indicators.note: fitted suggests parts put together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber installs a urinal that comes with a tap cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof sheet used to protect things, a kind of cover.

clue.text: Liberal whip, very independent at heart

indicators.note: at heart puts something in the middle of something else

parts.note: to lash is to whip
v is the abbreviation for very
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: The Liberal Party's whip is fiercely independent at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal whip' reads as a parliamentary officer; 'Liberal' is the definition in its generous sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, which matches lavish.

clue.text: 'Empty' chap wanting helping, that's Twist

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: guy is a chap; its first and last letters are kept
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Like Oliver Twist, an underfed boy asking for another helping.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T on Twist and 'wanting helping' evoke Oliver Twist asking for more, but Twist is the definition, a spinning motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyration is a whirling or spinning motion, so a twist or turn is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Military leader on rig forms part of UN

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
a rig is an assembly of equipment, a set of parts put together

explanation.surface: A general's rigging of something forms part of the United Nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The General Assembly is the main deliberative body of the United Nations, where every member state sits.

clue.text: Strikingly good non-stop chatter

definitions.meaning: second meaning: talking rapidly on and on

explanation.surface: Praising someone's excellent, unceasing conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a verb form, rattling (on), meaning chattering without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattling is a dated adjective meaning very good, and rattling on describes talking without pause.

clue.text: In effect, Russia's ex-leader

indicators.note: in says the wanted word lies inside the following words

parts.note: letters running across the end of effect and the start of Russia's

explanation.surface: A comment on Russia's former leader, in effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia's ex-leader' invites a Soviet name, but the hidden answer is Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Liz Truss led the Conservative Party and the UK government for seven weeks, so she is a former leader.

clue.text: One not in need of a bed is not to be considered long-suffering

definitions.text: One not in need of a bed

parts.note: an option that is out is ruled out, not to be considered
patient means enduring hardship without complaint

explanation.surface: A tolerant person who doesn't need a bed is dismissed from consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpatient attends hospital for treatment without being admitted to a ward overnight.

clue.text: To be established, turn up with Vernon

indicators.note: turn means rearrange, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: To get established, show up with Vernon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reads as the phrasal verb arrive; 'turn' alone is the signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unproven has not yet been shown true, so it remains to be established.

clue.text: Tense, out of practice — but reliable

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
rusty describes skills dulled by lack of use

explanation.surface: A nervous, rusty performer who can nonetheless be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty is an old-fashioned word for dependable, as in a trusty sidekick.

clue.text: Maybe New Zealand native dancing is as natural as giving up sex at first!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new order
giving up something means letting it go, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of sex, removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky claim that a dancing Kiwi finds celibacy as natural as anything.
explanation.walkthrough: One S comes out of 'is as natural as' before the remaining twelve letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealand lies in Australasia, so a New Zealander is one example of an Australasian; 'Maybe' flags the example.

clue.text: English town chasing crime boss

parts.note: hunting is chasing prey
a don is the head of a Mafia family

explanation.surface: An English town is hunting down a gangland leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, in eastern England, birthplace of Oliver Cromwell.

clue.text: See 18
Rock movement: country music, essentially, with edge

parts.note: a land is a country

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, the middle letter of the word

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter word
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: Describing rock music: a country song with an edgy feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' and 'country music' suggest genres; here rock is literal stone and country is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A landslip is a slide of earth and stone down a slope, literally rock on the move.

clue.text: County almost meets terrible end — right to give up

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the word's letters are jumbled
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Surrey is a county south of London
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A county side nearly comes to a bad end, and is right to concede.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to yield or hand over, which is what giving up means.

clue.text: New title has nothing about British book

indicators.note: new implies a fresh version, so the letters are made into something different

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
Br is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A newly published book whose title says nothing about Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is not a novel here: an opera's book is its text.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written text of an opera or musical, known in the theatre as its book.

clue.text: Cutlery, unless it's ground?

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, broken down and reformed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is it cutlery, unless it has been ground down?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'unless it is ground': the fodder is UNLESS IT and the 's stands for 'is', joining fodder to signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knives, forks and spoons are eating implements, and utensils is the general word for such tools.

clue.text: Circus feature draw: access to drink

parts.note: the ring is the arena where circus acts perform
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A circus attraction that draws people towards drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring pull is the metal tab you lift to open a can, giving access to the beverage inside.

clue.text: Package covering very loud sound restrictor

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: a bale is a bound bundle of goods
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Wrapping that muffles a very loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A baffle is a panel or device that deadens or deflects noise, as in a loudspeaker or exhaust.

clue.text: Working on research into Old English? The others don't stand a chance!

definitions.text: The others don't stand a chance!

indicators.note: into places one group of letters inside another

parts.note: OE is the standard abbreviation for Old English

indicators.note: working suggests material being worked over and reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholar of Old English so far ahead that rivals have no hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working on' reads as a phrasal verb; 'Working' alone is the signal and 'on' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse race is a contest with a certain winner, so every other competitor is hopeless.

clue.text: I'm surprised about church procuring prohibited drink

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: ooh is an exclamation of surprise
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A shocked reaction to a church getting hold of illegal liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about church' tempts a container round CH; instead 'about' reverses the exclamation, which then sits before CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for illicitly made liquor, the kind sold in America during Prohibition.

clue.text: Small parcel opening

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a parcel can be a lot, a portion of land or goods at auction

explanation.surface: Opening a small package.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is a narrow aperture, such as the gap for coins or letters.

clue.text: Road constructed by one-time expert

indicators.note: constructed means built up from parts in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A road built by a former expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-time' reads as former, but it splits into one and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and dexterous, so an expert performer is adroit.

clue.text: Round off Fed double cryptic puzzle

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the letters are scrambled
off means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a round shape is an O; this letter is removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to fool a double agent from the Fed with a cryptic puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' suggests an FBI agent, but it is just three letters of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To befuddle someone is to confuse or perplex them, as a verb meaning to puzzle.

clue.text: Elected politician recruits man on paper

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: recruits means takes in, so one part goes inside another

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A newly elected politician takes on a man, on paper at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle but perhaps not in practice, the sense of in theory.

clue.text: Time to import grass bloomers

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so one word is taken inside the other

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to grass and to rat both mean to inform on someone

explanation.surface: It is time to bring in grass seed for the flowering plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' and 'bloomers' suggest gardening; grass is British slang for inform, and bloomers is slang for blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing mistakes, and a bloomer is British slang for an embarrassing error.
